(a) Required. It shall be unlawful for any person to establish, operate or maintain, or permit to be established, operated or maintained upon any property owned or controlled by him, a trailer camp within the limits of the city without having first secured a license therefor. Such license shall expire one year from the date of issuance but may be renewed under the provisions of this chapter for additional periods of one year.
(b) Application. The application for such license or the renewal thereof shall be filed with the finance director, there will be no such fee charged for this license, for each unit in the existing or proposed camp. The application for a license or renewal thereof shall be made on such printed forms or other documents as may be furnished by the finance director and shall include the name and address of the owner of the tract and such a legal description of the premises, upon which the trailer camp is or will be located as will readily identify and definitely locate the premises. The application shall be accompanied by four copies of the camp plan showing the following, either existing or as proposed:
(1) The extent and area to be used for camp purposes.
(2) Roadways and driveways.
(3) Location of sites or units for trailer coaches.
(4) Location and number of sanitary conveniences, including toilets, washrooms, laundries and utility rooms to be used by occupants of units.
(5) Method and plan for sewage disposal.
(6) Method and plan for garbage removal.
(7) Plan for water supply.
(8) Plan for electrical lighting of the units.
(c) Recommendation; procedure. Before such license may be issued, there must be a favorable recommendation by the majority of the planning commission and the plan and premises must be inspected and approved by the chief of the fire department and the county health department. Upon obtaining the recommendation of the planning commission, the chief of the fire department, and the county health department, the license application shall be transmitted to the city council for public hearing. Such public hearing shall be conducted in the same manner as public hearings are conducted for rezoning or amendments to the zoning chapter, with the additional requirement that the city council shall consider and determine whether or not the proposed camp complies with the requirements contained in this chapter. After initial approval of the application and the granting of the license by the city council, the city council shall not be required to have a public hearing on the renewal of such license in subsequent years unless so requested by the planning commission, the chief of the fire department, or the county health department, or where a license previously issued shall have expired prior to the renewal thereof.
(d) Determination. Upon the conclusion of the public hearing, the city council shall determine whether or not to grant the license to the applicant.
(e) Limitations. Licenses issued under the terms of this chapter convey no right to erect any building, to do any plumbing work or to do any electrical work.
(Code 1986, § 21-2; Ord. No. O-90-07-19, 7-23-1990)

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Ashes means and includes the waste product from coal, wood, or other fuels used for cooking and heating from private residences.
Building refuse means solid waste generated from construction or demolition activities undertaken on property located within the corporate limits of the city.
Commercial solid waste means all types of solid waste generated by stores, offices, restaurants, warehouses, and other nonmanufacturing activities, excluding residential and industrial wastes.
Common continuing nuisance means a wrong that arises from unreasonable, unhealthful, unwarranted, or unlawful use by a person of his property, either real or personal, or from his improper, indecent or unlawful personal conduct, working an obstruction or an injury to the rights of the public, and producing material annoyance, inconvenience, discomfort or hurt to the public continuously or at frequent intervals.
Contractor means any person, and the agents and employees thereof, engaged in construction, electrical, mechanical, air conditioning, heating, plumbing, roofing, demolition, landscaping, masonry, allied work, nurserymen, and grounds keepers.
Debris means residue of any nature accumulating from the activities enumerated in the definition of contractor.
Garbage means all vegetable and animal matter, food, and other refuge from a kitchen, market, store, or elsewhere, including all matter that decays, attracts flies, and creates disagreeable odors.
Industrial refuse means waste materials from factories, processing plants, wholesale establishments, assembling plants, food processing wastes, cinders and ashes, lumber scraps, sawdust, shavings, and any other waste products from industrial and manufacturing processes.
Junk means old, scrap copper, brass, rope, rags, batteries, paper, trash, rubber debris, including tires, waste, junked, dismantled, or wrecked automobiles, trucks, or other vehicles or parts thereof, iron, steel, used household appliances, bottles, containers, boxes, barrels, and plastic.
Nuisance means stagnant water on-premises, loud or unusual noises which are detrimental to the public, including without limiting the foregoing, unusual loud disturbances in or around churches or multiple-family complexes such as loud music and other activities; dead or decaying matter which is odorous or capable of causing disease or annoyance to others; obstruction of a public street, highway, sidewalk; unused refrigerators, washing machines and other similar unused or unusable appliances; an accumulation of debris, objects, materials, and other conditions which may constitute a health, accident, or fire hazard, or which creates a blighting or deteriorating effect; any weeds, grasses, or plants other than trees, bushes, flowers, or other ornamental plants, growing to a height of 12 inches anywhere in the city; any vacant lot whereon debris is permitted to accumulate or vegetation, e.g., kudzu, is allowed to remain uncontrolled, in such a manner as to create a fire or other hazard to the public health, safety, or welfare; and any other condition constituting a nuisance under state law.
Rubbish means a variety of nonrecyclable household waste derived from places of residence and shall include paper, rags, plastics, cartons, boxes, broken glass bottles and jars, crockery, rubber, discarded clothing, and similar materials.
Waste means unwanted or discarded material including, but not limited to, ashes, building refuse, garbage, hazardous waste, industrial refuse, recyclable waste, rubbish, solid waste, and yard debris.
Wrong means a violation of public rights and duties which affect the community.
Yard debris means tree limbs, branches, stumps and logs, twigs, grass and shrub trimmings and clippings, bushes, weeds, leaves, and general yard and garden waste materials, and includes stone and dirt rakings and similar waste materials resulting from landscaping activities.
Yard trimmings means leaves, brush, grass clippings, shrub and tree prunings, discarded Christmas trees, nursery and greenhouse vegetative residuals, and vegetative matter resulting from landscaping development and maintenance, other than mining, agricultural and silvicultural operations.
(Ord. No. O-06-05-15, 5-18-2006)

(a) Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, the city shall be authorized to establish a procedure by which the city can acquire junked motor vehicles, as defined in section 58-47 of the Code, by issuing one-time credits on the city utility bill of the owner of the junked vehicle. Such provisions shall, at a minimum, provide as follows:
(1) That the city utilities director, or his designee, shall undertake, on a continuing basis, to locate, examine, and inventory all junked vehicles within the city. Such inventory shall be kept and maintained by the utilities director in his office and at such other location or locations as may be directed by the governing body of the city.
(2) With respect to any junked motor vehicle located upon the premises of a single-family or two-family residence, the utilities director shall determine the ownership of such motor vehicle, and such ownership shall be included in the inventory referred to above.
(3) The owner of the junked motor vehicle shall be contacted by the utilities director, or his designee, who shall be authorized to purchase the junked motor vehicle from the owner thereof in consideration of a $200.00 credit against the owner's city utility services bill.
(4) No such credit shall be provided until ownership of the junked motor vehicle is transferred to the city by certificate of title transfer or by bill of sale in the event that the junked motor vehicle is too old to require a certificate of title transfer. Any written transfer of a junked motor vehicle shall include, as part of the terms thereof, authority from the owner of the premises where the junked motor vehicle is located authorizing the city or its designee, to come upon the property where such junked motor vehicle is located and remove the junked motor vehicle by such means as may be deemed necessary by the city or its designee.
(5) Upon acquisition of the ownership of the junked motor vehicle, the utilities director shall be authorized to sell the junked motor vehicle to a recycling company determined by the utilities director to offer the most advantageous terms (financial and otherwise) to the city with respect to such purchase or purchases. Any sale to a recycling company may be made on a vehicle-by-vehicle basis or with respect to the sale of a group of vehicles. No public bidding shall be required for such sale.
(6) In the event that the utilities director is required to hire a tow truck company or companies to remove the junked motor vehicles from the premises where they are located, the utilities director shall be authorized to bid out such tow truck services on an annual basis, with the tow truck service being awarded to the lowest responsible bidder or bidders as determined by the utilities director. The utilities director shall also have the authority to terminate any such agreement with a tow truck service at any time due to the failure of the tow truck service to provide such service in a manner acceptable to the city. Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing herein shall be construed to prohibit the utilities director from awarding such bid to more than one tow truck service at a time and to use such tow truck services on a rotating basis as established by the utilities director if such procedure is determined to be in the best interest of the city.
(b) The city manager of the city, or her designee, shall be authorized to adopt further rules and regulations to implement and carry out the purposes and intent of this section.

The following acts, among others, are declared to be loud and disturbing noises in violation of this Code, but said enumeration shall not be deemed to be exclusive:
(1) Horns, signaling devices, etc. The sounding of any horn or signaling device on any automobile, motorcycle, or any other vehicle on any street or public place of the city, except as a danger warning; the creating by means of any such signaling device of any unreasonably loud or harsh sound; and the sounding of any such device for an unnecessary and unreasonable period of time; the use of any signaling device except one operated by hand or electricity; the use of any horn, whistle or other device operated by engine exhaust; or the use of any such signaling device when traffic is for any reason held up.
(2) Radios, phonographs, etc. The using, operating or permitting to be played, used or operated any radio receiving set, musical instrument, phonograph, or other machine or device for the purpose of producing or reproducing sound in such manner as to disturb the peace, quiet and comfort of the neighboring inhabitants or at any time with more volume than is necessary for convenient hearing for the person who is in the room, vehicle or chamber in which such machine or device is operated and who is a voluntary listener thereto. The operation of any such set, instrument, phonograph, machine or device between the hours of 11:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. in such a manner as to be plainly audible at a distance of 50 feet from the building, structure or vehicle in which it is located shall be prima facie evidence of a violation of this section.
(3) Yelling, shouting, etc. Yelling, shouting, hooting, whistling, or singing on public streets, particularly between the hours of 11:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. or at any time so as to annoy or disturb the quiet, comfort or repose of persons in any office, or any persons in the vicinity.
(4) Animals, birds, etc. The keeping of any animal or bird that by causing frequent or long continued noise shall disturb the comfort or repose of any persons in the vicinity.
(5) Steam whistles. The blowing of any locomotive steam whistle or steam whistle attached to any stationary boiler except to give notice of the time to begin or stop work or as a warning of fire or danger, or upon request of proper city authorities.
(6) Exhausts. The discharge into the open air of the exhaust of any steam engine, stationary internal combustion engine or motorboat or any other motor vehicle except through a muffler or other device which will effectively prevent loud or explosive noises therefrom.
(7) Defect in vehicle or load. The use of any automobile, motorcycle, or other vehicle so out of repair, so loaded or in such a manner as to create loud and unnecessary grating, grinding, rattling or other noise.
(8) Loading, unloading, opening boxes. The creating of a loud and excessive noise in connection with the loading or unloading of a vehicle or the opening or destruction of bales, boxes, crates and containers.
(9) Construction or repairing of building. The erection, including excavation, demolition, alteration or repair of any building other than between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., except in case of urgent necessity in the interest of public health and safety and then only with a permit from the building official, which permit may be granted for a period of not to exceed three days or less while the emergency continues and which permit may be renewed for periods of three days or less while the emergency continues. If the building inspector should determine that the public health and safety will not be impaired by the erection, demolition, alteration or repair of any building or the excavation of streets and highways within the hours of 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m., and if such official shall further determine that loss or inconvenience would result to any party in interest, such official may grant permission for such work to be done within the hours of 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m., upon application being made at the time the permit for the work is awarded or during the progress of the work.
(10) Schools, courts, churches, hospitals. The creation of any excessive noise on any street adjacent to any school, institution of learning, court or church, while many of the same is in use, or adjacent to any hospital, which unreasonably interferes with the workings of such institutions, or which disturbs or unduly annoys patients in the hospital, provided conspicuous signs are displayed in such streets indicating that the same is a school, hospital or court street.
(11) Hawkers, peddlers. The shouting and crying of wares, ringing bells or use of other noise making device by peddlers, hawkers and vendors which disturbs the peace and quiet of the neighborhood.
(12) Drums. The use of any drum or other instrument or device for the purpose of attracting attention by creation of noise to any performance, show or sale, except parcels, etc., authorized by proper authorities.
(13) Metal, rails, pillars and columns, transportation. The transportation of rails, pillars or columns of iron, steel or other material, over and along the streets and other public places upon carts, drays, cars, or trucks, which in any way disturbs the peace and quiet of persons in such streets or public places.
(14) Railroad operation. The causing, permitting or continuing any excessive, unnecessary and avoidable noise in the operation of a railroad locomotive or cars.
(15) Piledrivers, hammers, etc. The operation between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. of any piledriver, steamshovel, pneumatic hammer, derrick, steam or electric hoist or other appliances, the use of which is attended by loud or unusual noise.
(16) Blowers. The operation of any noise-creating blower or power fan or any internal combustion engine, the operation of which causes noise due to the explosion of the operating gases or fluids, unless the noise from such blower or fan is muffled and such engine is equipped with a muffler device sufficient to deaden such noise.
(17) Consumer fireworks. The ignition of consumer fireworks between the hours of 9:00 p.m. and 10:00 a.m. except during the days and times set out in O.C.G.A. §§ 25-10-2(b)(3)(B)(ii) and (iii).

(1) Accompanied by the minor's parent or guardian or an adult designated by the minor's parent or guardian;
(2) On an errand at the direction of the minor's parent or guardian or an adult designated by the minor's parent or guardian, without any detour or stop;
(3) In a motor vehicle involved in interstate travel;
(4) Engaged in an employment activity, or going to or returning home from an employment activity, without any detour or stop;
(5) Involved in an emergency. In this subsection the term "emergency" means an unforeseen combination of circumstances or the resulting state that calls for immediate action. The term includes, but is not limited to, a fire, a natural disaster, or automobile accident, or any situation requiring immediate action to prevent serious bodily injury or loss of life;
(6) Attending an official school, religious, or other recreational activity supervised by adults and sponsored by township, a civic organization, or another similar entity that takes responsibility for the minor, or going to or returning home from, without any detour or stop, an official school, religious, or other recreational activity supervised by adults and sponsored by the township, a civic organization, or another similar entity that takes responsibility for the minor;
(7) Exercising First Amendment rights protected by the United States Constitution such as the free exercise of religion, freedom of speech, and the right of assembly; or
(8) Married or had been married or had disabilities of minority removed in accordance with law.
(d) Business compliance required. It shall be unlawful for any person, firm, or corporation operating or having charge of any public business or place to knowingly permit, encourage, or allow the presence of minors under the age of 18 in such business or place between the hours of 11:00 a.m. and 5:30 a.m. Sunday through Thursday and between the hours of midnight and 5:30 a.m. Friday through Saturday in violation of subsection (b) of this section.

(f) Procedure upon violation. The following procedures shall be followed in connection with a violation of this section:
(1) Any police officer, upon finding a minor in violation of subsection (b) of this section, shall ascertain the name and address of such minor and then warn the minor that he or she is in violation of curfew and shall direct the minor to proceed at once to his home or usual place of abode. The police officer shall report the action to the chief of the city police department, who, in turn, shall notify the parents, guardian or person having custody or control of such minor.
(2) If such minor refuses to heed the warning or direction issued by a police officer, or refuses to give such police officer his correct name and address, or if the minor had been warned on a previous occasion that he or she is in violation of curfew, he or she shall be taken to the city police department and the parent, guardian or other adult person having the care and custody of such minor shall be notified to come and take charge of the minor. If the parent, guardian or other adult person above cannot be located or fails to come and take charge of the minor, the minor shall be released to the custody of juvenile authorities.
(g) Penalties. Each violation of this section shall constitute a separate offense. Any minor violating this section shall be dealt with in accordance with the juvenile court law of this state and procedures authorized by said law. In the event that any minor violates this section and such minor is not specifically covered or dealt with by the juvenile court law of this state, such minor shall be subject, after having been charged with the same and found guilty in the municipal court of the city, to punishment as provided in section 1-8. Any parent, guardian, or other adult person having legal care and custody of a minor and who permits said minor to violate this section shall be subject, after having been charged with the same and found guilty in the municipal court of the city, to punishment as provided in section 1-8.

960:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Aggregate sign area means the area of all signs on a parcel, excluding the area of one face of all double-faced signs.
Animated sign means a sign with action, motion, or changing colors that requires electrical energy. The term "animated sign" does not include signs that indicate only time, temperature, date, or any combination thereof.
Area of a sign or sign area means the smallest square, rectangle, triangle, circle, or combination thereof, which encompasses one face of the entire sign, inclusive of any border and trim, but excluding the base, apron, supports, and other structural members.
Awning sign means a sign located on a roof-like cover extending before a place as a shelter and which may be used in lieu of a wall sign.
Banner means a piece of fabric or similar material that is attached to a pole, enclosed in a frame, or mounted as a temporary sign device.
Billboard sign means a type of ground sign which is permitted in certain zoning districts as provided by this article, and which shall be a maximum of 35 feet in height and 240 square feet in sign face area, and which is greater than 100 square feet in sign face area. Billboards may be double-faced, and may include embellishments not exceeding an additional 50 square feet.
Directional sign means a sign dedicated to providing traffic direction such as enter, exit, drive through, etc. Limited to three feet in height and no larger than four square feet in sign area.
Double-faced sign means a sign which has two display areas placed back to back against each other or where the interior angle formed by the display areas is 60 degrees or less, where one face is designed to be seen from one direction and the other face from another direction.
Electronic message board (EMB). A form of changeable copy sign that is electrically activated and whose variable message or graphic presentation capability can by electronically programmed by computer from a remote location. EMBs typically use light emitting diodes (LEDs) as a lighting source.
Freestanding sign means a sign securely affixed to a support structure which is permanently attached to the ground and wholly independent of any building for support.
Hanging/shingle-type signs means a sign no larger than six square feet in area, with a clearance of seven feet eight inches above the sidewalk or ground. Such a sign shall be attached firmly and perpendicular to a building. Such a sign may be double-faced but may not be more than four inches thick.
Illuminated sign means a sign that has light cast upon the sign from a source either internal to the sign or from an external light source directed primarily toward such sign.
Monument sign means a permanent monument sign designed so that the base of the sign face is flush with the supporting base, and the supporting base is flush with the ground and extends the full width of the sign face and shall not exceed six feet in height, and 60 square feet in total area which shall include sign and structure. Such a sign shall require a building permit as provided in chapter 94 of the city Code in addition to any permits required under this chapter.
Mural means a painting or other work of art executed directly on an outer wall of a commercial building.
Nonconforming sign means any sign that does not conform to the provisions of this article that was legal at the time of its erection.
Parcel means a separate tax unit of real property on county real estate records.
Portable signs means a mobile/temporary electric or non-electric sign that is mounted on a trailer or trailer-type frame with wheels or skids or a portable wood or metal frame and is not permanently attached to the ground or to any building or other structure. The definition of "portable sign" does not include messages painted directly upon or attached by sticker or magnetic backing to a motor vehicle or placed within a motor vehicle such that it may be viewed from outside the vehicle through windows.
Roof sign means a sign attached to or supported by the roof of a building that extends above the immediately adjacent roofline of the building.
Shopping center means a commercial area apart from the central business district consisting of two or more businesses in one or more buildings in any linear or other arrangement and providing not less than 75 off-street parking spaces.
Sign means a device or representation for visual communication that is used for the purpose of bringing the subject thereof to the attention of others.
Streamers means a sign consisting of narrow strips of plastic, cloth, or similar material used to direct attention to a building, sign, or physical location on a temporary or permanent basis.
Strip center means a commercial area apart from the central business district consisting of two or more businesses in one or more buildings in any linear or other arrangement and providing at least 25 off-street parking spaces.
Temporary sign means a sign of a nonpermanent nature.
Wall sign means a sign fastened, placed or painted upon or parallel to the exterior wall of the structure itself, and may be located on multiple walls provided each sign faces a street or parking lot. The term "wall sign" does not include a mural as defined in the city Code.
Window cling sign means a sign that depicts the appearance of the building upon possible future occupancy. Window cling signs may include information about the sale or lease of the building, but are not considered real estate signs under section 74-3.
Window sign means a sign installed flush with or on a window and intended to be viewed from the outside, and cannot exceed 30 percent of the available window space. Window signs shall not count towards the maximum aggregate sign area.

(a) Procedure. The city shall deny permits to applicants that submit applications for signs that do not comply with the provisions of this chapter, incomplete applications, and applications containing any false material statements. Violation of any provision of this chapter will be grounds for terminating a permit granted by the city for the erection of a sign. Should it be determined that a sign permit was issued pursuant to an incomplete application or an application containing a false material statement, or that a permit has been erroneously issued in violation of this chapter, the building risk management office shall revoke the permit. Should the city deny a permit, the reasons for the denial are to be stated inwriting and mailed by certified mail, return receipt requested, or via hand delivery to the address on the permit application on or before the thirtieth business day after the city's receipt of the application. Any application denied and later resubmitted shall be deemed to have been submitted on the date of resubmission, instead of the date of the original submission. No permit shall be denied or revoked, except for due cause as hereinafter defined, and the applicant is granted a public hearing before the board. The applicant will be given ten days' written notice of the time, place, and purpose of the hearing, with a statement of the reason for the denial of the permit application, or the revocation of a permit. The term "due cause" means the violation of the provisions of this chapter, state or federal law related to signage, or the submission of an incomplete application or an application containing false material statements.
(b) Appeal; final decision by city council. An individual whose permit application has been denied, or a permittee whose permit has been revoked, may appeal the decision to the board to the city council, provided that they file written notice of an appeal with the city clerk within ten business days of the decision. Such appeal shall be considered by the city council at the next city council meeting held after the city's receipt of the written notice of appeal, provided that notice of appeal is received a minimum of two full business days before the meeting. If the appeal is not heard at such meeting, it shall be heard at the next regular meeting of the city council thereafter. The city council shall make a final decision no later than 30 days from the date of the hearing. An applicant denied a permit by final decision of the city council shall have a right to appeal the decision of the council to the superior court.
(c) Petition for writ of certiorari by denied applicant. In the event that an individual whose permit has been denied or revoked is dissatisfied with the decision of the city council, he or she may petition for writ of certiorari to the superior court as provided by law.

(a) Freestanding signs. No freestanding sign may be located within 30 feet of the intersection of street right-of-way lines extended.

984:

No external or internal illumination that causes confusion with or distraction from any traffic signal or safety device shall be permitted.

(a) Multiple-message signs are those which change the message or copy on the sign face mechanically or electronically by movement or rotation of panels or slates, or by changing electronic display on the sign face. Except as expressly provided in this article for multiple-message billboards, such signs are not permitted in the C-3, R-1, R-2, R-3, and R-3A zoning districts and the historic district, but are permitted in all other zoning districts.
(b) No multiple-message sign may change its message or copy, or any pictures or images that are part of the message, more frequently than once every minute, provided that multiple-message billboards shall be allowed to change the copy or images that are part of the message not more frequently than once every ten seconds.
(c) When the message of a multiple-message sign is changed mechanically, it shall be accomplished in three seconds or less. When the message of a multiple-message sign is changed in an electronic manner, through the use of light emitting diodes, back lighting or other light source, the transition shall occur within two seconds.
(d) Except as expressly provided in this article in regards to billboards, the portion of the sign face of a multiple-message sign which accommodates multiple-messages shall not exceed 50 percent of the total sign face area and may not change its message or copy, or any pictures or images that are part of the message, more frequently than once every minute; the remaining portion shall be static.
(e) When any multiple-message sign is located within 250 feet of any residential district, the display of multiple-messages shall discontinue between the hours of 11:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. and the sign shall be static and not display more than one message during that period.
(f) Multiple-message signs which are illuminated or which use electronic lighting to display message shall be subject to the restrictions and limitation applicable to illumination in this article.
(g) There shall be located no more than one multiple-message sign per lot, and such sign shall be permitted only on a ground sign or freestanding structure, and not on any wall sign or window sign.
(h) The total number of multiple-message billboards within the city shall be limited to eight sign faces. After the adoption of this article, new multiple message billboards shall only be permitted when both of the following location requirements are met:
(1) The proposed multiple-message billboard is to be erected on an existing billboard sign structure as of the date of the adoption of this article or at the location of and as a replacement for such an existing billboard sign structures. A list of such existing billboard sign structures known to the city is attached (by reference) as exhibit A to the ordinance adopting this article, and identified as "Billboards existing in the City of Americus, Georgia, as of July, 2015;" and
(2) The proposed multiple-message billboard will be located facing one of the following designated public right-of-way, which are deemed by the city council to be the only rights-of-way within the city where multiple-message billboards are appropriate.
(i) Multiple-message billboards constructed after the adoption of this article shall be located at least 5,000 feet from existing billboards using a multiple-message sign face, measured from the base of the billboard along the street frontage to the base of the nearest existing billboard using a multiple-message sign face on the same side of the street, and 3,000 feet from any existing billboard using a multiple-message sign face, measured along the shortest straight-line from sign structure to sign structure.
(j) No multiple-message sign shall be permitted in any historic district of the city.
(Ord. No. O-2015-9, Exh. A, 6-18-2015; Ord. No. O-2021-4, 3-18-2021)

(a) EMBs are permitted only in non-residential zoning districts and are not permitted in the downtown or historic districts, except as otherwise provided by the city Code.
(b) EMBs shall be set back 150 feet from a residential dwelling unit, provided however that the set back distance may be reduced at the discretion of the director of planning development if the residential dwelling unit is fully screened from the EMB.
(c) EMBs may be an element of a monument, freestanding, or window sign. Any sign containing an EMB shall be subject to the provisions of this section in addition to the provisions of any other section of this chapter governing the type of sign containing said EMB.
(d) An EMB display shall remain unchanged for a minimum of 15 seconds.
(e) EMBs displaying animated and/or video images are prohibited.
(f) Intensity of light.
(1) The EMB shall be required to be equipped with an automatic dimming photocell which shall automatically adjust the EMB's brightness based on ambient light conditions.
(2) The brightness level shall not increase by more than 0.3-foot candles (or 3.23 lumens per square meter or lux), over ambient lighting levels, as measured using a footcandle meter at a pre-set distance.
(3) The procedure and distances for measurement of brightness shall be as established by the International Sign Association's "Recommended Night-Time Brightness Levels for On-Premise Electronic Message Centers."
(g) Default control.
(1) EMBs shall be equipped to freeze the display in one position if a malfunction occurs.
(2) EMBs shall be equipped with a means to immediately discontinue the display if it malfunctions.
(3) The owner of the EMB must immediately stop the display when notified by the community development director that the sign is not complying with the standards of this section.

(a) In order to comply with the city's liability insurance carrier, the city shall require that all sponsors of special activities or commercial video or film crews carry liability insurance with coverage of at least $1,000,000.00, except for class I; low-hazard activities as defined in subsection (c) of this section. Where liability insurance is required, an activity sponsor shall be required to provide a valid certificate of insurance naming the city as an additional or named insured prior to the activity. The city manager may require higher levels of insurance based upon risk factors and past experience.
(b) The special activity review committee shall include the city manager, the city clerk, the finance director, and the community development director. The special activity review committee is intended to provide a review of proposed special activities and a risk control guide for the handling of any increased liability on the part of the city associated with special activities. Special activities are defined as activities which are not directly related to the day-to-day operations of the city, but which may occur on premises owned or controlled by the city. The special activity review committee shall make recommendations to the city manager regarding approval of the special activity, liability insurance requirements, and regarding any additional requirements that the committee deems it appropriate to be placed upon any special activity as a condition of the issuance of a permit for such activity.
(c) It shall be the policy of the city council to not routinely require insurance coverage for activities classified by the special activity review committee as class I; low-hazard. These would be activities that include no physical activity by participants and no substantial exposure to spectators. This waiver of the insurance requirements is meant to cover small gatherings or ceremonies that do not involve more than 50 people, are limited to passive participation by the public, and require no city services. All other activities are required to provide insurance as outlined in this policy.
(d) In making its recommendations to the city manager regarding each special activity permit, the special activity review committee may recommend additional requirements as a condition of permit issuance. Such additional requirements may include, but shall not necessarily be limited to, specific staffing levels for police, fire, public works, or other personnel in connection with the activity. Expenses incurred by the city in compliance with such requirements shall be billed to and paid by the sponsoring organization. Agreement by the sponsoring organization to pay such additional expenses may be made a condition of the issuance of the permit by the city manager.
(e) The special activity review committee will review each special activity permit application received and assess the potential liability risk of the city, based upon the following categories:
(1) Class I; low-hazard activities involve no physical activity by participants and no substantial exposure to spectators. Examples of activities in this category include, but are not limited to, meetings, seminars, social gatherings, theatrical performances, and weddings.
(2) Class II; moderate-hazard activities involve limited physical activity by participants and no substantial exposure to spectators. Activities in this category include, but are not limited to, downtown celebrations, dances, animal shows, political rallies, and picnics.
(3) Class III; high-hazard activities major participation and/or moderate exposure to spectators. Activities in this category include, but are not limited to, marathons or running races and circuses or carnivals.
(4) Class IV; severe-hazard activities involve substantial exposure to participants and/or spectators. Examples of activities in this category include, but are not limited to, rock concerts, vehicle races, and fireworks displays.
(f) The city manager shall consider the recommendations of the special activity review committee in connection with the approval or disapproval of the proposed special activity. The city manager shall be authorized to accept or reject the recommendations of the committee regarding approval of the proposed permit and regarding the placing of additional requirements, including liability insurance requirements, upon the activity as a condition for the issuance of the permit. The city manager shall also be authorized to place such additional restrictions or requirements as part of the permit as the city manager deems appropriate and in the best interest of the city. The city manager shall also be authorized to require a member or members of the special activity review committee to be available to meet with activity organizers to review any special conditions and to ensure that all such special conditions are met before or during the course of the activity. Some special activities may require that a member of the special activity review committee be on site during the course of the special activity.

1039:
With respect to the naming of a new street owned by the city and located within the corporate limits of the City of Americus, the governing body shall be required to follow the following procedures with respect to the naming of such new street:
(1) By application of a citizen or group of citizens.
a. A citizen or group of city citizens may submit an application to name a new street hereunder. Such application shall be on forms prescribed by the city clerk. Such application shall not be considered unless at least 75 percent of the persons owning real property abutting such new street submit a written application to the city clerk requesting that such street be named a particular name.
b. Such application shall be accompanied by a nonrefundable fee of $100.00, which is intended to cover administrative and other costs which are anticipated to be incurred by the city in connection with its consideration of the application. Such application fee shall be deposited into the general fund of the city.
c. The governing body of the city shall consider such application and act thereon in accord with this division no later than 90 calendar days after the date of submission of such application to the city clerk. In the event that the governing body does not act upon the application prior to the expiration of such 90 calendar day period, then the street shall be automatically renamed as requested in the application.
d. Upon receipt of the application by the city clerk, the city clerk shall proceed to validate the application. The city clerk shall validate the application by verifying that the proper number of signatures is contained on the application and that the persons signing the application are owners of real property abutting said street as required by this division. In the event that the city clerk determines that the application is invalid for any reason, or that the application does not contain sufficient signatures, the application shall be returned to the person or persons submitting such application, and it shall not be subject to further consideration by the governing body until such time as a new application is submitted and the city clerk validates the new application.
e. In determining the required percentage of the persons signing such application in connection with the validation thereof, where property abutting such street is owned by more than one person, the signature of only one such owner shall be counted in calculating such 75 percent. In addition, persons who rent or lease real property abutting such street may sign such application, but their signatures shall not be counted toward the 75 percent threshold for submission of the application to the governing body. Signatures on any such application signed more than 90 calendar days prior to the date of submission of the application to the city clerk shall be invalid and shall not be counted toward the 75 percent threshold. In the event that more than one application for naming a new street is presented to the city clerk, the city clerk shall validate such applications in the order received. The first application validated by the city clerk shall be presented to the governing body first, and only if the resolution to approve the application is denied shall the city clerk present the second or subsequent validated application to the governing body.
f. The application shall be in such form as established by the city clerk. At a minimum, the application shall indicate thereon the location of the street, the proposed name of the street, the printed name, street address, and signature of each property owner signing such application, and the date that each property owner signed the application. In addition, each such application shall include therewith a written statement which provides, in succinct detail, the reasons for the proposed street naming in honor of a particular person or business listed in the application. In providing such written statement, the criteria to be considered by the governing body regarding the naming of such street as more particularly established in this division shall be specifically addressed by the application in such written statement accompanying the street naming application. In addition, the application shall also list any public announcement or public recognition request that should accompany any official street naming ceremony undertaken by the city in connection with the naming of such street.
g. In the event that the city clerk determines that the application is valid, then prior to the submission of the application to the governing body, the city clerk shall undertake the following:
1. Provide notification of the application to and compile for review by the governing body responses to the application from the following:
i. All city agencies and departments, including, but not limited to; city police, city fire and EMS, city GIS system personnel, city building risk management risk department, and other city agencies or departments that the clerk deems appropriate;
ii. All other local, state, or national agencies which the city clerk determines may be affected by the naming of the street;
iii. All schools located in the immediate vicinity of the street;
iv. Any other persons or entities the city clerk deems, in his or her sole discretion, should receive notice of the proposed street naming.
2. Review existing public records for the purpose of establishing that the proposed street name does not duplicate any existing street name and is not confusingly similar to any existing street name in Americus or Sumter County.
h. Upon the completion of the foregoing, the city clerk shall be required to place consideration of the application on the agenda for the city council meeting occurring in the calendar month after the month in which the application was finally validated. Nothing herein shall be construed to prohibit the tabling of such proposal by the governing body, but in no event shall consideration of such proposal by the city council be delayed beyond 90 calendar days after the validated application was filed with the city clerk.
i. Prior to the governing body considering or voting upon such application, the governing body shall hold a public hearing regarding such application. Notice of such public hearing shall be published once in the city's legal organ no later than the day prior to the date of the public hearing. Such public notice shall advise the public regarding the application, the proposed new street name, and the time and place of the scheduled public hearing before the governing body. Such public hearing shall be conducted with the same formality as that required of public hearings in connection with zoning and rezoning matters before the governing body. Upon conclusion of the public hearing, the governing body shall be authorized to vote on the application.
j. In the event that the application is approved by an appropriate resolution of the governing body, the name of the street shall take effect at such time as is determined by the governing body in such resolution.
k. Upon adoption of the resolution by the governing body, the city clerk shall undertake the following:
1. Provide written notice to each property owner owning property abutting the street of the official name of the street as approved by the governing body;
2. Provide written notice of the name of the street to the United States Postal Service;
3. Provide written notice of the name of the street to the emergency 911 system in effect for the geographical area including the City of Americus.
l. Within 60 calendar days of the effective date of the resolution adopting the street name, the city utilities director shall have fabricated and installed appropriate signage regarding the name of the street at such locations as deemed appropriate by the utilities director.
(2) By the professional staff of the city.
The professional staff of the city, or a member of the city council, may submit an application to name a new street. The procedures to be followed by the governing body in the event that such an application is submitted shall be the same procedures as previously outlined in this section, except that no application fee shall be required, and the application shall not require the signatures of 75 percent of the persons owning real property abutting the new street.
(Ord. No. O-07-03-12, § 18-102, 3-22-2007)

(Ord. No. O-07-03-11, § 18-201, 3-22-2007)
1052:
The following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, as follows:
City block is the smallest area that is surrounded by public streets within the incorporated area of the city.
Lot owners means the owner or owners of record of each lot abutting a proposed sidewalk, whether or not there is constructed on such lot a dwelling, house, commercial building or other structure. Such term shall include both personal and business owners of such lots of record.
Petition means a petition as more particularly described in section 78-203 of this article.
(Ord. No. O-07-03-11, § 18-202, 3-22-2007)
1053:
(a) Whenever any lot owner or owners located within the corporate limits of the city desire to request the city to install a sidewalk fronting the property owned by such lot owner or owners along one or more sides of a city block, then such lot owner or owners shall notify the city clerk, who shall provide the lot owner or owners with a pre-printed petition, which petition shall be for the purpose of ascertaining the level of support for the installation of such sidewalk. At the time of providing the petition to the lot owner or owners, the city clerk shall determine an estimated installation cost of the proposed sidewalk, which cost shall be assessed to each lot owner in a prorated amount as established in this article, and such estimated cost shall be provided to the lot owner or owners requesting the application.
(b) Such petition shall have typed thereon a title, which shall be "Petition Requesting the City of Americus to Install a Sidewalk Along the ___________ Side of ___________ Street from ___________ Street to ___________ Street." There shall further be typed thereon the following statement at the top of each page of the petition:
The undersigned, by signing this petition, do hereby request the City of Americus to install a sidewalk as described above. The undersigned have been informed and do understand that if at least 75 percent of the record owners of lots abutting such proposed sidewalk sign this petition, the governing body of the city may authorize the installation of such sidewalk, and each record owner of a lot or lots abutting said sidewalk shall be required to pay the pro-rated cost of installation of such sidewalk as established by city ordinance.
(c) Such petition shall thereafter have spaces for the printed name and address, the legal signature, and the date of signing for each lot owner who signs such petition. Such petition shall be returned to the city clerk within 90 calendar days of the date that the petition was delivered by the city clerk to the lot owner or owners requesting such petition. No such petition shall be returned to or accepted by the city clerk until at least 75 percent of the record lot owners abutting the proposed sidewalk shall have signed the petition. For purposes of ascertaining the 75 percent threshold, the following shall apply:
(1) A lot owner may be counted as signing the petition only once, regardless of the number of lots such lot owner may own abutting said sidewalk.
(2) Where property is owned by more than one person, the signature of only one such owner shall be counted in calculating such 75 percent.
(3) Persons who rent or lease property abutting such proposed sidewalk may sign such petition, but their signatures shall not be counted toward the 75 percent threshold.
(4) Where the lot owner is a corporation or other legal entity, the petition shall only be signed by an authorized officer or agent of the corporation.
(d) Upon submission of said petition as a single petition to the city clerk, the city clerk shall cause the signatures thereon to be verified. The city clerk shall validate the petition by verifying that the proper number of signatures is contained on the petition and that the persons signing the petition are owners of real property abutting said proposed sidewalk as required by this article. In the event that the city clerk determines that the petition is invalid for any reason, or if the application does not contain sufficient signatures, the application shall be returned to the person or persons submitting such application, and it shall not be subject to further consideration by the governing body until such time as a new application is submitted and the city clerk validates the new application. Any persons who are not record
owners of lots abutting the proposed sidewalk, or who are otherwise not authorized to sign such petition or have their signatures counted, shall have their names stricken from the petition and shall not be counted for purposes of ascertaining the 75 percent threshold.
(e) If, after verification of the signatures, the city clerk determines that at least 75 percent of the lot owners owning real property abutting the proposed sidewalk have signed the petition, then said petition shall be presented to the governing body of the city at its next regular monthly meeting for consideration. In the event that the petition contains the properly verified signatures of at least 75 percent of the persons owning real property abutting the proposed sidewalk, the city council shall be authorized to approve the installation of the sidewalk, but the city council shall not be required to approve such installation.
(f) If the installation of such sidewalk is approved by the city council, the appropriate city departments shall proceed with the installation of such sidewalk, which installation shall be performed in accord with applicable building and other codes.
(g) The city shall provide all labor and materials required for the installation of the sidewalk. At the conclusion of the installation, the city clerk shall determine the actual total installation cost incurred by the city, including, but not limited to; the cost of labor, materials, right-of-way acquisition, surveys, and engineering costs. Such cost shall be determined within 30 calendar days of the completion of the installation. The finance director shall then determine the cost of the installation per linear foot and shall cause each lot owner abutting such subdivision to be billed an amount equal to such cost per linear foot times the number of linear feet owned by such lot owner abutting the installed sidewalk. Such bills shall be paid by the lot owners within 30 days of submission by the city. In the event that it is requested by one or more lot owners and approved by the governing body, and in lieu of payment of such cost of installation in one payment, as to any lot owner or owners so requesting, the city shall be authorized to bill each lot owner for such lot owner's prorated cost over a 12-month period; provided, however, that any lot owner requesting to be billed over a 12-month period shall also pay interest equal to one percent per month on the unpaid principal balance until all payments are paid in full. The sale of the lot prior to the lot owner's payment of such prorated cost shall not relieve the lot owner of the obligation to pay such cost in full as required by this article. Failure to pay any installment when due shall entitle the city to terminate utility services to the lot owner in the same manner as if the lot owner had failed to pay a city utility bill. Nothing herein shall prohibit the city from including the billing for the pro-rata share of the installation of such sidewalk to the lot owners in the lot owner's monthly utility bill.

1066:

Any building erected in violation of this section shall be deemed an unlawful structure, and the building official, city attorney or other official designated by the city council may bring appropriate action to enjoin such erection or cause it to be vacated or removed.

1070:
(a) The procedure for formal review and approval of a subdivision plat shall consist of the following three separate steps:
(1) The subdivider should consult early and informally with the community development director and/or other city technical staff for advice and assistance before the preparation of the preliminary sketch plat and its formal application for approval. This will enable the subdivider to become thoroughly familiar with these standards, the major street plan and other official plans or public improvements that might affect the area. Such informal review should prevent unnecessary and costly revisions.
(2) Prior to the making of any street improvement, or installations of utilities, the developer shall submit to the planning commission a preliminary plat of the proposed subdivision. After receiving the planning commission's approval of the preliminary plat and full concurrence and approval by the city, the developer may then proceed to grade the streets and install all improvements required by this chapter and any other applicable city ordinances. In lieu of the completion of all improvements prior to submission of the final plat, the developer may post a bond with the city, or certified check, in an amount and with surety satisfactory to the city and conditions satisfactory to the city, providing for and securing to the city the actual construction and installation of such improvements within a period specified by the planning commission and stated in the bond.
(3) After completion of the physical development of the subdivision or the posting of a bond or certified check to guarantee the same, the developer shall submit to the planning commission a final plat together with any required certificates. The final plat, along with any deed restrictions, becomes the instrument to be recorded in the office of the clerk of the superior court of this county.
(b) No final subdivision plat shall be approved by the planning commission or accepted for record by the office of the clerk of the superior court of this county until the required improvements listed shall be constructed in satisfactory manner and approved by the appropriate approving agent.
(Code 1986, § 19-20; Ord. No. O-97-03-05, 3-20-1997)
1071:
(a) At least ten days prior to the regular meeting of the planning commission the subdivider shall submit to the building official's office three copies of the plat of the proposed subdivision drawn to a scale of not less than one inch equals 100 feet, along with a receipt for the filing fee from the finance director.
(b) The preliminary plat shall meet the minimum standards of design and general requirements for the construction of public improvements as set forth in article III of this chapter and shall give the following information insofar as possible:
(1) Description:
a. Proposed name of subdivision.
b. Name and address of subdivider.
c. Graphic scale, north point and date. The north point shall be identified as magnetic, true, or grid north.
d. Location sketch map showing the relationship of the subdivision site to the surrounding area, including directions and distances to readily identifiable landmarks in the surrounding area.
e. Acreage to be subdivided.
(2) Existing conditions:
a. Topography by contours at vertical intervals of not more than two feet, or as determined necessary by the city utilities director, when a new street is involved in a subdivision, including outline of wooded areas and classifications of land.
b. Zoning district classification on land to be subdivided and of adjoining land.
c. Names and addresses of adjoining property owners or subdivisions.
d. In case of resubdivision, a copy of existing plat with proposed resubdivision superimposed thereon.
e. Location of streams, lakes and swamps and land subject to flood as determined from past history of flooding (listed on appropriate FEMA map).
f. Location of existing and platted property lines, location, width and names of all platted roads, railroads, utility rights-of-way, public areas, existing buildings or structures.
g. Existing sewers, water mains, drains, culverts or other underground facilities within the tract or within the right-of-way of boundary roads, with sizes, grades and invert elevations from public records, or from field surveys, or other sources. All sizes and data on all utilities shall be provided.
h. Certification by the county health officer when individual sewage disposal or water systems are to be installed.
(3) Proposed conditions:
a. Layout of roads, alleys and public crosswalks, with widths, road names or designations.
b. Layout of all lots and the area of each lot, including building setback lines and lot divisions with scaled dimensions and utility easements with width and use on all lots.
c. Preliminary plan of all utilities to be constructed.
d. Designation of all land to be reserved or dedicated for public use.
(c) Within 30 days after submission of the preliminary plat, the planning commission shall review it and indicate its approval, disapproval, or approval subject to listed modifications, as a basis for preparation of the final plat. If a plat is disapproved, reasons for such disapproval will be stated in the records of the planning commission. Failure of the planning commission to act on the preliminary sketch within 30 days will be deemed approval of this plat, unless the developer agrees to an extension of time.
(d) Approval of the preliminary plat by the planning commission shall not constitute acceptance of the final plat and shall not be indicated on the preliminary plat.
(e) The approval of the preliminary plat shall lapse until a final plat based thereon is submitted within one year from the date of such approval, unless an extension of time is applied for and granted by the planning commission.
(f) After the planning commission has reviewed and acted on the preliminary plat, one copy will be returned to the developer, one copy will go to the building official's office and one copy will be retained in the records of the planning commission.
(g) After the planning commission has approved the preliminary plat, construction plans should be submitted to the building official and include the following:
(1) Layout of roads, alleys and public crosswalks, with widths, road names or designations, grades and cross sections.
(2) Preliminary plan of sanitary sewers with grades, service, pipe size and points of discharge, together with certified copy of all load design factors and computations.
(3) Preliminary plan of storm drainage system with glade, pipe size and location of outlet, together with certified copy of all design factors and computations.
(4) Preliminary plan of water supply system with pipe sizes and location of hydrants, valves and all appurtenances.
(Code 1986, § 19-21; Ord. No. O-97-03-05, 3-20-1997; Ord. No. O-04-12-33, 12-16-2004)
1072:
(a) At least ten days prior to the regular meeting of the planning commission the subdivider shall submit to the building official's office an original on reproducible Mylar or vellum, and three copies, of the final plat. The final plat shall conform substantially to the preliminary plat as approved and, if desired by the subdivider, it may constitute only that portion of the preliminary plat which such developer proposes to record and develop at the time, provided, however, that such portion conforms to all requirements of these standards.
(b) The original shall be drawn to a scale of not less than one inch equals 100 feet on reproducible Mylar or vellum and shall correspond to plat book dimensions. It shall be the developer's responsibility to provide the clerk of superior court with a plat that will fit in the plat book/cabinet. When more than one sheet is required, an index sheet of the same size shall be filed showing the entire subdivision with sheets lettered in alphabetical order as a key.
(c) When the plat has been approved, the original will be returned to the developer with the approval of the planning commission certified thereon for filing with the clerk of the superior court of this county; one copy will be returned to the developer for such developer's records; one copy will be forwarded to the building official's office and one copy will be returned in the records of the planning commission.
(d) The planning commission shall approve or disapprove this final plat within 30 days after its submission to that body. Failure of the planning commission to act on this final plat within these 30 days shall be deemed approval of it. If the plat is disapproved, the grounds for disapproval shall be stated upon the records of the planning commission.
(e) Approval of the final plat by the planning commission shall not constitute acceptance by the public of the dedication of any streets or public ways or ground.
(f) The final plat shall comply with the plat act and shall give the following information:
(1) Certification that the applicant is the landowner, all parties with mortgage or lien interest to be included, and that applicant dedicates street rights-of-way and any sites for public use.
(2) Certification by a licensed surveyor to the accuracy of survey and plat and placement of monuments.
(3) Certification by the proper city officials that the developer has complied with the following: All improvements have been installed in accord with the requirements of this chapter and other applicable city ordinances.
(4) Protective covenants or deed restrictions, if any, shall be placed directly on the final plat or attached thereto in form for recording.
(5) Certificate on the plat to be signed by the secretary of the planning commission when the plat has been given final approval by the planning commission.
(Code 1986, § 19-22; Ord. No. O-97-03-05, 3-20-1997; Ord. No. O-99-02-08, 2-18-1999)

1076:
(a) Land which the planning commission has found to be unsuitable for subdivision due to flooding, bad drainage, steep slopes, rock formations, or other features likely to be harmful to the safety, health, and general welfare of the future residents shall not be subdivided unless adequate methods approved by the planning commission are formulated by the developer for meeting the problems created by the subdivision of such land.
(b) Land subject to flooding shall not be platted for residential occupancy or for such other uses, as will not comply with chapter 34, article II, the danger to health, life and property unless such land is not to be used as a building site. In applying this provision, land liable to flooding as determined from past history shall be considered subject to flood. Fill shall not be used to raise the land in areas subject to flood unless the fill proposed does not restrict the flow of water and unduly increase flood heights.
